answer: Each agent stakes ferrous tokens—hard, physical-anchered collateral—before it can vote, so a sybil flock spins up a thousand wallets only to find each one must lock value and accrue reputation slowly, and cost scales linearly while payoff stays flat. The fable ends the same every time: wallets multiply, but worth never does. Attacker's bottleneck becomes capital per identity, not identities spawned, since zenith reputation demands months of honest uptime no clone can shortcut.
